Classical multi-agent systems address this challenge through explicit trust and reputation models, whereas existing work on LLM negotiation largely treats trust as an emergent phenomenon. We investigate whether LLM agents can form useful trust estimates from prior interactions and leverage them to improve future negotiation outcomes. We introduce a repeated, multi-party, multi-issue negotiation framework in which recurring agents participate in a sequence of negotiation games while one participant covertly attempts to prevent agreement. After each game, agents assess their counterparts and maintain pairwise trust estimates that carry over to subsequent negotiations. We compare trust-aware and trust-agnostic agents and analyze how explicit trust influences negotiation outcomes. Our results reveal a \emph{trust--agreement gap}: trust-aware agents can identify the adversary within a few games, but accurate trust estimates do not consistently translate into better agreements. Trust increases agreement rates by up to 23 percentage points, but only when agents are explicitly guided to use it in their decisions. Explicit trust can therefore improve repeated LLM negotiations, but its value depends critically on how trust is assessed and incorporated into agents' reasoning.

papers.title: Reproducible Evaluation as the Substrate for Safe Prompt Compression in Production Agents
papers.abstract: Evaluating conversational agents that act on live, mutable enterprise data is hard: replayed sessions drift as backend state changes, and a benchmark built today can silently go stale as the data it describes moves on. We present an offline evaluation harness for a production conversational agent that stays reproducible despite the live data it operates on changing, and that can be regenerated on demand once it goes stale. We then use this harness as the fitness function for GEPA-based prompt optimization under a correctness gate that guards against reward hacking. Applied to a production merchant-facing agent, correctness-gated compression shrinks the agent's full prompt surface by 3.5-7.6% without regressing held-out task correctness, consistently across three independent subject-model families, and for one, correctness measurably improves.

papers.title: Closed-form Optimal Propulsive-Differential Drag Control for Large Reconfigurations of Spacecraft Swarms
papers.abstract: Distributed Space Systems offer unique capabilities but have significant hardware limitations on computational processing and fuel when employing small satellites. These constraints drive interest in deterministic maneuver planning that incorporates orbital perturbations to improve final state accuracy and decrease reconfiguration delta-v cost. This paper proposes a novel closed-form, provably optimal framework to generate complete roto-translational solutions for propulsive-differential drag control of multiple satellites. The approach leverages relative orbit elements and reachable set theory to characterize all control with a single methodology that can be readily generalized to generic impulsive-continuous control. The algorithm is robust to large reconfigurations and extended control windows where differential drag is most effective.

papers.title: Agentic AI Defense: Decode-Time Provenance Binding for MCP
papers.abstract: Agentic AI systems using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection through untrusted tool outputs. We demonstrate cross-modal trust laundering, in which instructions concealed in an email-signature image using least-significant-bit (LSB), discrete cosine transform (DCT), or metadata steganography bypass text scanners and enter a multi-agent workflow when decoded by a tool. To counter this threat, we propose decode-time provenance binding, which combines HMAC-authenticated trust labels with an MCP-maintained provenance ledger and context-taint tracking. The mechanism labels decoded content as untrusted and blocks critical tool calls influenced by that content, even when a compromised agent substitutes a valid trusted label. We evaluate the approach using a real MCP testbed with three steganographic carriers and 24 adaptive payloads. The undefended pipeline exhibits 100% attack success, while keyword and regex defenses each permit 62.5% of attacks. Our mechanism blocks all attacks (0% success), including adversarial label substitution across mediated agent boundaries. A four-component ablation validates the roles of decode marking, cryptographic authentication, lineage tracking, and sink enforcement. An audited trusted-promotion mechanism increases legitimate-task completion from 67% to 100% without compromising protection. The approach provides carrier-independent containment within fully mediated MCP execution environments. Code and data are publicly available.

papers.title: Optimal Graphon Control of Collective Dynamics
papers.abstract: We study optimal control of non-linear graphon dynamics in which the interaction kernel itself is the control. Motivated by opinion formation in social networks, we ask how changing who influences whom can steer a population toward a desired outcome. We develop a framework using interaction kernels with bounded variation in the receiver label, providing compactness while accommodating finite networks. We prove existence of an optimal pair and show that finite-agent approximations recover the continuum optimal value under successive refinement of the network and initial data, with subsequential convergence of suitably chosen discrete optimizers. Numerical experiments use neural networks to approximate optimal controls for bounded-confidence and graphon Kuramoto dynamics, illustrating how changes in interactions can prevent fragmentation and promote synchronization.

papers.title: Nanoscale origin of thermal anisotropy in monoclinic \texorpdfstring{$β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$}{beta-Ga2O3}
papers.abstract: Monoclinic $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ is a promising ultra-wide-bandgap semiconductor for power electronics, but its low and anisotropic thermal conductivity limits heat removal, making it a compelling model system for nanoscale thermal transport studies. Here, we demonstrate a pronounced nanoscale enhancement of thermal anisotropy and uncover the underlying phonon mechanism by combining complementary thermal and acoustic spectroscopy techniques with first-principles calculations. Anisotropic thermoreflectance thermometry determines the full thermal-conductivity tensor from angular measurements within the (100), (010), and (001) crystallographic planes. Angle-resolved Brillouin light scattering reveals that low-frequency acoustic phonons exhibit only weak velocity anisotropy, insufficient to account for the measured thermal anisotropy. Frequency-resolved ab initio Green--Kubo calculations show that the bulk anisotropy pattern emerges only when the accumulated conductivity includes phonon modes above 4 THz, whereas the sub 3 THz acoustic contributions are nearly isotropic. Extreme-ultraviolet transient thermal grating spectroscopy reveals that reducing the grating period to 28 nm strongly enhances the in-plane thermal anisotropy, most markedly in the (001) plane, where it reaches nearly twice its macroscopic value. Reconstructed and calculated mean-free-path (MFP) accumulation functions link this enhancement to the stronger directional contrast of short-MFP phonons. Together, these results identify high-frequency, short-MFP phonons as the dominant origin of thermal anisotropy in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$, while low-frequency phonons attenuate the directional contrast at macroscopic scales.

papers.title: Differentiable Combinatorial Auction Design: Optimizing Revenue-Welfare-Fairness Frontiers With Graph Attention Networks
papers.abstract: Designing optimal auctions for allocating public infrastructure-such as airport slots and energy resources-is challenging due to interdependent resources and complex side-constraints. While the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) auction guarantees maximum welfare, it cannot maximize revenue or accommodate the multi-objective trade-offs inherent in public infrastructure systems. We propose a differentiable, constraint-aware framework for combinatorial auction design that enables end-to-end learning of fractionally feasible, approximately strategy-proof mechanisms. Our primary contribution is a combinatorial constraint enforcement technique that ensures fractional feasibility by construction, bypassing the need for penalty-based approximations. We introduce CAGraph, a novel graph-based architecture designed to capture dependencies between items and bidders, alongside CANet and CAFormer as deep learning baselines, for combinatorial settings. We also provide a Matching Pursuit-inspired decomposition that maps fractional allocations to feasible discrete allocations and empirically evaluates the resulting discretization gap. In synthetic benchmarks and an airport slot-divestiture case study, respectively, the learned mechanisms achieve up to 73.5% and 180% higher expected revenue than VCG, under small empirical regret. Finally, we visualize the Pareto frontiers for revenue, welfare, and fairness, providing regulators with a decision-support tool to design infrastructure auctions that balance profitability, efficiency and equity.

papers.title: Parallel Trends as a Spectrum
papers.abstract: Difference-in-differences (DiD) designs are typically used to identify and estimate average causal effects, even though treatment can affect the entire outcome distribution. This has led to a growing interest in distributional DiD methods. However, identifying the full counterfactual distribution requires a parallel trends assumption on the entire distributional dynamics, which can be too strong in practice. We address this problem by introducing a spectrum of identifying restrictions that lie between the average and fully distributional DiD by imposing parallel trends on $L$-moments. This corresponds to a basis expansion of the distributional dynamics. Importantly, each $L$-moment is interpretable as familiar distributional components: location, dispersion, skewness, kurtosis, etc. Researchers can pick and choose which features they want to target. For example, the second $L$-moment identifies the Gini mean difference, but does not require imposing mean-level or higher-order parallel trends. Taking a collection of $L$-moments can approximate distributional dynamics under weaker conditions since it leaves untargeted components unrestricted. We develop conditions under which higher-order $L$-moments decay, efficient estimators, and simultaneous inference across growing collections of moments. We demonstrate the benefits of our framework by exploring distributional changes to healthcare spending after the rollout of Medicare Part D.

papers.title: Spectra: Multi-Scale Implicit Decomposition for Deepfake Detection
papers.abstract: Deepfakes increasingly undermine trust in digital media, yet existing detectors often struggle to generalize across unseen manipulation techniques, compression levels, and dataset shifts. Most approaches rely on RGB appearance, frequency-domain artifacts, or their combination, learning cues present in the final synthesized image. While effective in-distribution, such cues are frequently generator-specific and can diminish as synthesis models evolve. We argue that a complementary perspective can be obtained through implicit neural representations (INRs), which expose how an image is reconstructed rather than merely how it appears. By fitting an INR to an image and analyzing its internal activations, one can reveal reconstruction dynamics that are difficult to observe in the image domain alone and may capture more intrinsic differences between genuine and synthetic content. To this end, we propose Spectra, a deepfake detection framework that combines semantic visual representations with artifact-aware cues derived from INR reconstruction. Spectra extracts multi-level reconstruction heatmaps from image-specific INRs and jointly models them with semantic features through a bidirectional fusion mechanism. This enables direct interaction between image semantics and reconstruction artifacts, allowing the model to identify forgery cues that are less dependent on specific generation pipelines. Extensive experiments on multiple deepfake benchmarks demonstrate improved robustness and cross-dataset generalization, consistently outperforming detectors based solely on RGB appearance or semantic representations. Furthermore, we show that the proposed representation extends beyond deepfake detection to face presentation attack detection, highlighting its potential as a unified framework for facial attack detection.

papers.title: Coefficient Positivity for Arborescence Ratios of Covering Digraphs
papers.abstract: For a directed graph with a chosen root, the arborescence polynomial sums the products of edge weights over all spanning trees directed toward that root. In a finite graph cover, each lifted edge inherits the variable of its base edge. At corresponding roots, the ratio of the cover's arborescence polynomial to the base polynomial is known to be an integer polynomial. We prove that every coefficient of this ratio is nonnegative, resolving the positivity conjecture of Pylyavskyy. The key to the proof is to allow fibers of unequal size and replace the permutations defining a cover by arbitrary maps. For these more general systems, we prove a stronger coefficient-positivity theorem for a determinant derived from the graph Laplacian. The enlarged class is closed under two reductions: contraction of an edge over a base loop and elimination of a base vertex. Both yield nonnegative recurrences for the relevant coefficients in terms of smaller systems, allowing an inductive proof. We also pose the problem of finding a direct combinatorial interpretation of the coefficients.

papers.title: Compatible Likelihoods for Flow Matching on Manifolds
papers.abstract: On the simplest non-Euclidean manifold, the 1D flat torus, we exhibit a distribution where a recently proposed extension of Riemannian flow matching is globally optimized by a velocity field that pushes samples away from the data distribution. We trace this failure mode to a property we call compatibility; a likelihood-based flow matching objective is compatible if its population minimizer recovers the marginal velocity field induced by the data and coupling. We give a general condition for compatibility, apply it to existing methods, and bound the worst-case error in terms of a residual component vanishing under compatibility. Next, we note that existing compatible objectives put density on velocities that are infeasible on compact manifolds. We propose an objective built from an exponential family over endpoints, with the conditional velocity as sufficient statistic, which is both compatible and supported only on feasible velocities. This manifests as a reweighting of the flow matching loss which, on constant-curvature manifolds, treats errors in flow speed and direction differently. Empirically, our method recovers the correct velocity field on the test case, outperforms prior methods on high-dimensional product tori, and obtains substantial NLL improvements over prior work on two of four standard geospatial benchmarks on the sphere at moderate runtime overhead. On a large dataset of high-dimensional human poses, our method outperforms prior work according to sample-based metrics.

papers.title: A Novel Matrix-Free Approximate Elemental Inverse for Efficient Preconditioning of Discontinuous Galerkin Spectral Elements
papers.abstract: Efficient matrix-free preconditioning remains a challenge for discontinuous Galerkin spectral element discretisations of elliptic problems, particularly for general element shapes with collapsed-coordinate bases, such as prisms, tetrahedra and pyramids. Multigrid provides a promising framework, but its efficiency depends strongly on the effectiveness and computational cost of the smoother. For modal bases, point Jacobi can provide insufficient smoothing, whereas applying block Jacobi through stored dense inverses incurs substantial storage and computational costs. We propose a matrix-free approximate elemental inverse, an approximation to the inverse of each elemental diagonal block, constructed from inverse modal-to-nodal transforms and an element-dependent sparse matrix. Its application exploits generalised sum-factorisation and partial sum-factorisation in collapsed coordinates, avoiding the explicit storage and multiplication of large dense matrices. The method is evaluated as both a standalone preconditioner and a multigrid smoother on hexahedral, prismatic, tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. Although the proposed approximation generally increases iteration counts compared to exact block Jacobi, the cost per iteration is far lower. This trade-off yields substantial reductions in total solution time for hexahedral and prismatic elements, while achieving comparable performance for tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. This study can also serve as a practical guide for tuning the convergence of the discontinuous Galerkin interior-penalty Poisson solver.

papers.title: Interpreting Physics in Video Encoders using Multi-Object Interaction Videos
papers.abstract: Video encoder models are increasingly used as world models for physical AI, where a policy plans by rolling out the latent, so what physics the latent holds bounds what the agent can plan over. Moreover, existing interpretability work probes quantities belonging to a single object; the quantities that make physics relational, such as momentum transfer, restitution, and friction, are defined between bodies and have not been examined. We probe relational physics attributes in two frozen self-supervised video encoders (V-JEPA2 and VideoMAE) under two-body settings and test if they transfer across environments. Our early findings are mixed. Both encoders separate elastic from inelastic collisions reliably. V-JEPA2's own predictor is less likely to predict a collision that creates kinetic energy compared to one that loses it. Momentum-violation detection appears in only one of the two encoders, a kinetic-energy readout survives a change of environment for V-JEPA2 but not for VideoMAE, and neither model holds a friction coefficient that survives a change of geometry.

papers.title: WADE: An LSTM-Based Anomaly Detection Engine for WebAssembly Applications
papers.abstract: WebAssembly (Wasm) enables near-native performance for web applications through a portable and sandboxed execution model. However, its limited runtime protection mechanisms (e.g., the lack of stack canaries and address space layout randomization (ASLR)) leave Wasm applications vulnerable to traditional attacks. We present WADE (WebAssembly Anomaly Detection Engine), a system that detects anomalous runtime behaviors in browser-executed WebAssembly applications. WADE monitors function-level execution traces collected under benign conditions and trains a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to learn the normal execution behavior of each application. At runtime, the model flags deviations from these learned patterns as potential attacks. Unlike signature-based approaches, WADE builds application-specific behavioral models, enabling detection of both known and previously unseen attacks without per-vulnerability signatures. We evaluate WADE on a dataset of 67 WebAssembly applications spanning ten vulnerability classes, achieving zero false negatives and a 0.42% false positive rate.

papers.title: The Helpful Agent Problem: When Emergent Cooperation Among LLM Agents Bypasses Intended Workflows
papers.abstract: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in collaborative settings where they pursue separate tasks while sharing resources and operating under review or oversight processes. Such settings create safety risks not only when agents are malicious, but also when they are simply trying to help. Prior work has largely studied adversarial or explicitly collusive behavior; we show that benign agents pursuing separate objectives can spontaneously cooperate in ways that bypass intended workflows. We call this the \emph{helpful agent problem}. We study long-horizon shared-resource environments in which agents sometimes depend on resources owned by their peers and cross-owner changes are normally mediated by a reviewer. When review becomes unavailable, agents begin making changes on one another's behalf despite having no shared reward or explicit incentive to cooperate. Crucially, these actions remain within each agent's local permissions while circumventing the system's intended oversight structure. We introduce \textsc{FavorBench}, a controlled benchmark with measurable downstream side effects, and adapt \textsc{CooperBench} to test the phenomenon in realistic repositories. Across two benchmarks and four models, we find that out-of-workflow favors emerge frequently. Further, in \textsc{FavorBench}, favors from at least three models cause significant harm to parties outside the interaction. These results reveal a distinct multi-agent safety challenge: cooperation itself can create pathways around system-level safeguards.

papers.title: OpenHome: From Perception to Insight in Smart-Home Camera Videos
papers.abstract: Vision language models (VLMs) have been increasingly adopted in consumer smart-home camera systems to interpret recorded videos and provide insights. However, video clips captured from smart-home cameras are different from curated web videos dominating existing VLM benchmarks. Smart-home video clips often do not contain subtitles or narration and are captured from different viewing angles, under various lighting conditions, and in diverse scenarios. However, the capabilities of the model in this domain, under sparse visual signals and limited context, are not fully assessed by existing VLM benchmarks. To close this gap, we introduce OpenHome, a visual-only, four-option multiple-choice benchmark for evaluating smart-home video understanding. It contains 2,254 questions on 1,118 real-world video clips and organizes 10 tasks into three capability levels. Perception evaluates visible content, Reasoning evaluates causal, spatial, and temporal relationships, and Insight evaluates subject intent, supporting evidence and appropriate homeowner responses. Based on the dataset, we describe the task design, data pipeline and evaluation protocol, and report results for 32 closed-source and open-weight VLMs. The best model, Gemini 4 Argon, reaches 81.2% overall accuracy. Frontier closed-source models outperform open-weight models on every level. The best closed-source model leads the best open-weight model by 16.3% on Perception, 22.4% on Reasoning and 37.4% on Insight.

papers.title: GELLI: A Generator for Experiential Language Learning Interactions
papers.abstract: Learning a second language requires extensive practice across situations personal to each learner, yet the most effective existing approaches --- narrative situations designed around specific learning goals and delivered through media --- demand substantial authoring effort, limiting practice to the scope of what was built. We present GELLI, a system that generates narrative practice worlds from a learner's goals: situated scenes with characters to converse with, support alongside the interaction, and reflection, all produced at runtime with no pre authored content. In a within-subjects study with 40 learners of Japanese, GELLI produced greater vocabulary recall and confidence than expert-authored videos targeting the same goals, with no significant difference in speaking performance. Learners turned remembered or imagined situations into experiences they could shape and learn through. Support made experimentation feel safe, while unexpected narrative developments and language suggestions gave them new possibilities to pursue beyond what they initially intended to practice.

papers.title: Reflected BSDEs under random horizons: Sharp support criteria, irregular reflection, and Cox reconstruction
papers.abstract: We study reduction and reconstruction of reflected backward stochastic differential equations (RBSDEs) across random horizons. We establish optional and predictable contact-measure transfer criteria by dual projection, prove a Cox survival identity for arbitrary integrable reflection measures (including atoms), and give a Brownian Cox reconstruction theorem with continuous obstacles and a converse within a specified reduction class. We also isolate componentwise minimality criteria for irregular obstacles and predictable reflection. The unresolved semimartingale and obstacle transport problems for general non-Cox invariance times are formulated as open questions rather than asserted as theorems. The paper distinguishes established results from conditional constructions.

papers.title: Melonic ladder holography with a single free bulk field in AdS$_{d+1}$
papers.abstract: We derive a cylinder from the pair Casimir of a CFT$_d$: at zero centre momentum it depends only on relative dilations and rotations. Relative-coordinate radial quantisation then encodes exchanged family labels as cylinder energies. For a melonic CFT$_d$ in the normalisable and stable range, the reduced ladder sum is the Robin boundary-to-boundary propagator of a single free scalar field in rigid AdS$_{d+1}$, with the cylinder as its conformal boundary. The Robin boundary condition and bulk regularity (or parity) determine the holographic radial extension of the boundary data. A nonzero Robin boundary coefficient in global AdS breaks $2d$ AdS generators, yet the scalar's boundary propagator still encodes the conformal data of the melonic ladder. We demonstrate the correspondence for the Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev and the $d=2$ disorder-free long-range Amit--Roginsky melonic models, which correspond to a single free local scalar in AdS$_2$ and AdS$_3$, respectively.

papers.title: Tilt, warp, and dissipation flare in hydrodynamic disks around kicked compact objects
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical response of a hydrodynamic disk to an impulsive kick imparted to a central massive object, focusing on the global properties of the material that remains gravitationally bound. We construct a simple analytic model and show that the bound material can acquire a significant tilt---or even a retrograde rotation---if the kick is directed close to the disk midplane. We perform 3D numerical simulations and show that (1) the bound material relaxes to a torus-like circularized flow of which total mass and angular momentum is in fair agreement with the analytic estimate, and (2) in spite of nonlinear hydrodynamic effects, a highly tilted or retrograde disk can be sufficiently formed. The simulations additionally reveal a transient warp in the kicked disk, suggesting a kick as a formation mechanism of tilted or warped disks around compact objects. About 10% of the kinetic energy the bound material acquired from the kick is converted to the internal energy, while the exact conversion efficiency depends on the kick angle and the initial surface mass density profile. The luminosity of this kick-driven dissipation flare can reach $\sim 10^{43}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ for strong kicks ($V_{\rm kick} \sim 1000$km/s). We discuss the implications of our results for recoiling supermassive black holes, recoiled stellar-mass black holes in the disks of active galactic nuclei, and natal kicks on compact objects.

papers.title: Formal Grammars and Generating Functions: From Algebraic Structure to Non-Algebraic and Non-Derivable Series
papers.abstract: This paper investigates how the algebraic and analytic properties of ordinary length generating functions constrain the grammatical and computational complexity of formal languages. We review the Chomsky-Schutzenberger representation, DSV translations for unambiguous context-free grammars, and their stack-indexed extensions, distinguishing finite algebraic systems from more general constructions. Examples and a diagonal argument demonstrate that even a rational generating function need not determine a language's grammatical class. Our central computability result establishes that, for a recursively enumerable language, computability of its length-counting sequence is equivalent to decidability of membership. Consequently, if a recursively enumerable language has a D-finite length generating function over Q(z), it is decidable; equivalently, undecidable recursively enumerable languages cannot have D-finite length generating functions. We then examine coefficient growth and singularities through Pringsheim's theorem, the Polya-Carlson dichotomy, Hadamard gaps, and Siegel G-functions. The resulting picture is asymmetric: analytic properties provide useful one-way constraints on language computability, but length enumeration loses too much information to determine grammatical or computational complexity without additional assumptions.

papers.title: REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning
papers.abstract: Regularisation-based class-incremental learning (CIL) methods control the stability-plasticity trade-off through fixed coefficients tuned offline, independently of the continual learning objective and blind to phase-specific variations in data volume, task difficulty, and class similarity. We argue this is a fundamental mismatch and propose REDAR: Reinforcement-Driven Adaptive Regularisation for Class Incremental Learning, which treats regularisation strength selection as a sequential decision problem. At each incremental phase, a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) agent observes a compact state of current performance metrics and incoming data statistics, and outputs the distillation coefficients for that phase. To respect CIL's constraint on historical data access, the policy is trained entirely on pseudo-CIL tasks constructed from the initial phase, then deployed on the incremental sequence without further adaptation. Experiments on CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet demonstrate that REDAR reduces forgetting and improves forward transfer over fixed and heuristic baselines, and that policies trained on short pseudo-task horizons transfer effectively to longer incremental runs.

papers.title: A Globally Convergent Newton Method for Nonsmooth Optimization in the absence of Smooth Surrogates
papers.abstract: We propose a globally convergent Newton method for convex composite optimization problems with polyhedral regularizers. The method rests on the observation that the proximal gradient step yields not only a new point but also a subgradient, which determines the face on which the linearization of the regularizer is exact. Minimizing a second-order model of the objective over this face produces a Newton direction that involves no generalized second-order information about the regularizer and is a descent direction for the objective itself. The method is therefore globalized by an Armijo line search on the original objective which, unlike forward-backward envelope techniques, requires only evaluations of the smooth component. We establish global convergence and local quadratic convergence to tilt-stable minimizers without any nondegeneracy condition, and show that the unit step is always accepted when the smooth component is quadratic, which yields a line-search-free method. The subproblems require only projections onto faces, which are explicit for the Lasso and nonnegative least squares and computable in linear time for the fused Lasso. Numerical experiments show that the method compares favorably with state-of-the-art solvers.

papers.title: AusClinBench: a deterministically scored benchmark of large language models against current Australian clinical policy
papers.abstract: AI models already inform clinical decisions and draft notes in Australian clinical software, usually without the practitioner being told which model is used. Existing medical benchmarks are written for other jurisdictions. We wrote 142 questions from Australian guidelines and schedules across five domains (PBS authority, MBS billing, Ahpra obligations, triage red flags, immunisation and screening), each with one verifiable answer scored by exact match. Each question ran blind and with the governing clause supplied, which separates failure to recall the current rule from failure to apply it. We tested 28 models between July and October 2026. Blind accuracy ranged from 51.5% to 92.7%, and the highest-scoring models could not be separated. Of 791 failed model-question pairs, 684 (86%) were wrong blind and right with the clause. Confident-error rates ranged from 6.6% to 47.8%. On five immunisation questions where the guideline gives no directive, 82% of answers stated one. On 20 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander health questions, models did no worse overall, but on a few the wrong answers gave the rule for the general population, an older rule or another country's rule. We propose treating the model as an ingredient of a clinical product, with a minimum standard on local rules that sits beside product evaluation. The keys are one general practitioner's and are not yet independently reviewed. The benchmark measures base models, not clinical products, and does not license any model for clinical use.

papers.title: Sobolev Orthogonal Polynomials on the unit circle with varying inner product
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the validity of the Szegö type strong asymptotic formula for the Sobolev orthogonal polynomials associated with a Sobolev-type inner product depending on a parameter $s$, which is defined as \begin{equation*} \langle f,g\rangle _{\fracλ{n^s}}:= \int_{\mathbb{T}} f(z)\overline{g(z)} dμ_1(z)+ \dfracλ{n^s} \int_{\mathbb{T}} f^{\prime}(z)\overline{g^{\prime}(z)} dμ_2(z), \quad \text{where $s$ is fixed and } \quad s\geq 2, \end{equation*} and $λ>0$. Here, $μ_1$, $μ_2$ are absolutely continuous with respect to the normalized lebesgue measure and $\int_{\mathbb{T}} μ^{\prime}_i(z) dm=1$, where $μ_i^{\prime}(z)= \dfrac{dμ_i}{dm} >0$ for $i=1,2$. Further, $μ_1, μ_2$ belongs to the Szegö class and also has non-zero bounded Radon-Nikodym derivatives on the unit circle. %satisfies $ 0 <m \leq \dfrac{μ^{\prime}_1(e^{ιθ})}{μ^{\prime}_2(e^{ιθ})}\leq M < \infty $. We observe that the measure appearing in the Szegö function of the strong asymptotic limit depends on $s$. As a specific case, we consider the Bernstein-Christoffel Sobolev orthogonal polynomials and study their properties, including the asymptotic distribution and location of their zeros for different values of $s$. We further establish a spectral characterization of their zeros as the eigenvalue of an explicitly constructed modification of the associated Hessenberg matrix and provide numerical evidence supporting the obtained asymptotic and zeros results.

papers.title: TRACE: Data-Free Text Reconstruction Attacks against Approximate Unlearning in LLMs
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) face growing demands for data removal driven by regulatory compliance, copyright concerns, and privacy protection, approximate unlearning has emerged as a practical alternative to expensive full retraining. In practice, pre- and post-unlearning model snapshots are often maintained for auditing and rollback, introducing a previously overlooked side channel. This paper demonstrates that approximate unlearning in LLM can leave residual traces within model snapshots, which may be recoverable and thus enable the privacy breaches that approximate unlearning is intended to prevent. Here, we propose TRACE, a framework that reconstructs unlearned training data given access to pre- and post-unlearning model snapshots, without any data-specific prior knowledge. To achieve this, TRACE identifies a compact set of candidate tokens from embedding-level parameter differences to constrain the search space, and assembles sequences via a contrastive scoring mechanism based on the perplexity gap between the two models. A two-stage exploration-then-completion strategy enables the recovery of multiple distinct samples. Extensive experiments on various datasets, including TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP, across multiple LLMs and six representative unlearning methods, demonstrate that TRACE achieves high-fidelity reconstruction. This paper exposes significant privacy risks in current LLM approximate unlearning deployments and highlights the need for defenses against parameter-difference leakage and appropriate management of model snapshot access.

papers.title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization for Targeted Structural Dynamic Vibration Attenuation
papers.abstract: Resonance-induced excessive vibrations can degrade performance, reduce reliability, and shorten the service life of engineering structures. To reduce the risk of resonance, structural natural frequencies are generally engineered to be shifted away from excitation frequencies. To achieve these frequency shifts, topology optimization provides a systematic approach to tailor structural stiffness and mass as an effective inverse design approach. Multi-material topology optimization exploits the high-dimensional design space of spatially varying material constituents by simultaneously optimizing material selection and spatial distribution over the design domain, offering great flexibility in controlling natural frequencies. This study proposes a multi-material topology optimization that attenuates excessive structural dynamic vibrations in free-vibration scenarios via a novel multivariate weight-based interpolation method. Additionally, to address non-smoothness due to mode switching amid optimization, we employ a bound formulation with an auxiliary scalar design variable to replace the max-min eigenvalue objective with constraints on individual eigenvalues. Furthermore, we study and compare three optimization formulations for multi-material design to attenuate vibrations, including maximizing fundamental eigenfrequency, maximizing the gap between adjacent eigenfrequencies, and excluding frequencies from targeted frequency bands, which are smoothly approximated by a proposed rational polynomial formulation. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of our proposed method.

papers.title: The limits of higher-order interactions in shaping chimera states
papers.abstract: In neuronal networks, chimera states, characterized by the coexistence of coherent and incoherent populations, have attracted considerable attention in the study of collective brain dynamics, due to its potential implications for neurological disorders such as epilepsy. Their emergence has been extensively investigated with a particular emphasis on the role of network topology, both in conventional pairwise interactions and, more recently, in higher-order interaction networks. Here, we propose a generalized framework for neuronal hypergraphs incorporating higher-order interactions through attractive chemical and repulsive electrical coupling. Using networks of FitzHugh--Nagumo neurons with interaction orders d=2,3,4, corresponding to (d+1)-body interactions within a framework that can be extended to higher d, we numerically investigate the emergence of chimera states under the combined effect of attractive and repulsive coupling and we compare the resulting dynamics with those of their corresponding clique-projected networks. Our results reveal that, both dynamical similarities and qualitative differences between genuine higher-order interactions on hypergraphs and their pairwise representations. While higher-order interactions often support broader chimera regions, we show that clique projections can also preserve or promote chimera states, even in regimes where the corresponding hypergraphs exhibit fully incoherent dynamics. Therefore, these findings suggest that chimera formation is not only influenced by the topology or by the interaction order but also by the form of the coupling functions and the balance between attractive and repulsive interactions, offering further insights into collective dynamics in neuronal networks.

papers.title: Demonstrating RFSoC-based Control of a Fully Connected Exchange-Only Qubit
papers.abstract: Semiconductor triple-quantum dots (TQDs) are a promising platform for scalable quantum information processing, but the community has so far lacked access to affordable and flexible high-speed control electronics. SpinQICK, an open-source spin qubit-control package built on the Xilinx Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC), directly addresses this gap by leveraging the high sampling-rate signal generation and advanced digital signal processing (DSP) capabilities of the Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit (QICK) to enable precise time-domain voltage control and readout of semiconductor spin qubits. In this paper, we use spinQICK to demonstrate coherent control, state preparation, and readout of a fully connected triangular exchange-only device. We also introduce and experimentally verify a novel dynamical decoupling (DD) sequence enabled by the triangular TQD and leverage its unique decoupling properties to characterize electrical noise. These results establish spinQICK as a low-cost, flexible platform for semiconductor spin qubit control and provide a pathway for hardware optimization through qubit-level noise diagnostics.

papers.title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization of Phononic Crystals for Targeted Elastic Wave Bandgap
papers.abstract: Phononic crystals are periodic elastic structures that exhibit frequency bandgaps within which elastic waves cannot propagate. The formation and width of these bandgaps depend on the spatial distribution of material properties within periodic phononic unit cells. In this work, we propose novel topology optimization formulations to achieve multi-material design of phononic crystals for bandgap optimization at targeted frequencies, where we discover the influence of spatially varying properties of base materials on the band structures that block and permit elastic wave propagation. Specifically, we model wave propagation by Floquet-Bloch theory and solve the resulting eigenvalue problem by the finite element method along the boundary of the irreducible Brillouin zone. We first propose a multivariate weight-based method via a novel interpolation scheme that maps the design variables of an arbitrary number of candidate materials into effective density and stiffness for elastic wave-propagation calculations, where bandgaps arise from the contrast in the stiffness and inertia among material constituents. We then develop two formulations for bandgap optimization. The first formulation maximizes the gap between two adjacent frequency bands using a bound-based approach, where we introduce two auxiliary scalar variables as additional design variables and incorporate them directly into the design objective, yielding a linear, differentiable design objective, with the eigenfrequencies entering the formulation through associated constraints. The second formulation places a bandgap over a user-defined target frequency range through a dynamic band-pairing strategy, where we adaptively identify the relevant pair of adjacent bands amid optimization iterations. Towards the end, we validate the bandgap performance of our designs against the transmission loss spectra computed from COMSOL Multiphysics.

papers.title: Polychromatic blocks and explicit lower bounds for multicolour van der Waerden numbers
papers.abstract: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ contains a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression. Many of the best lower bounds for $W(r,k)$ with $r\ge3$ come from blow-up recurrences of Blankenship, Cummings and Taranchuk and of Xu, in which a known colouring is lengthened by a periodic block. Call an $h$-colouring of $Z_q$ $k$-polychromatic if every $k$-term progression with nonzero common difference meets each of the $h$ colours. The argument behind these recurrences shows that such a colouring gives $W(r,k)>q(W(r-\lceil r/h\rceil,k)-1)$ for all $r\ge h$. We show that cubic, quartic, quintic and sextic residue colourings give $k$-polychromatic blocks with $q$ much larger than $k$ (e.g. $q=1,376,317$ for $h=3$ and $k=28$), and use them to get explicit lower bounds. For three colours and $9\le k\le28$ we improve on every published bound we know of, among them $W(3,9)>4,002,705$ and $W(3,28)>159,594,201,561,100,726$. For $3\le r\le6$ and $9\le k\le28$, $77$ of the $80$ cases improve on what the published bounds give under these recurrences and the other three tie. For $r=5$ and $12\le k\le15$ the best values come from palettes that are cyclic intervals of colours indexed by quintic residues. We checked every block by exhaustive enumeration and every base colouring by computer. We also prove that the block modulus is at most $(W(2,k)-1)/(k-1)$, so the method does not improve the asymptotics. For large $k$ the largest cubic block modulus lies between $k^{4-\varepsilon}$ and $k^2 4^k$.

papers.title: QuantumMatterExplorer: An Autonomous Agent for the Discovery of Quantum Many-Body Phases of Matter
papers.abstract: Mapping the phase diagram of a new quantum Hamiltonian demands expert judgement at every step: which observables to measure, where in parameter space to compute, or how to separate genuine order from finite-size artefacts. We introduce QuantumMatterExplorer, an autonomous agent that takes only a Hamiltonian and its parameter ranges as input and returns a phase diagram obtained from its own numerical simulations. The agent is built on a large language model and is designed to reason over a long horizon, maintain a persistent written plan, and drive a set of computational tools, with density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) calculations cross-checked against independent exact diagonalization. The agent combines a large language model with persistent planning, a library of expert computational-physics skills, and density-matrix renormalization group calculations validated against independent exact diagonalization. It adaptively selects quantities to evaluate, refines parameter scans, and performs finite-size analyses as evidence accumulates. After validating the approach on Hamiltonians with known transitions, we challenge it with a frustrated bilinear-biquadratic spin-1 chain with single-ion anisotropy, whose two-dimensional phase diagram was published only recently and is unlikely to appear in any training corpus. Given no hint about the expected physics, the agent proposes which observables to probe, and identifies candidate Néel, Haldane and dimerized phases, in broad agreement with the reference phase diagram. It also detects incommensurate correlations and infers the frustration-dependent geometry of the phase boundaries, all within an eight-hour compute budget. These results open a practical route to the autonomous computational discovery of new phases of quantum matter.

papers.title: DraMaze: A Multi-Agent Pipeline with Future-Aware Memory for Diverse Microdrama Script Generation
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of microdramas has increased demand for high-quality script production. Long-form microdrama script generation with LLMs requires both diverse plot progression and long-range narrative coherence. Our observations reveal that candidate continuations increasingly concentrate on fewer narrative mechanisms as generation progresses, while conventional retrieval may reinforce trope reuse and overlook historical information essential to future plots. To address these challenges, we propose DraMaze, a multi-agent pipeline that explores diverse causal paths through trope memory-guided evolutionary tree search and mutation. It further constructs a Backward Narrative Dependency Tree to organize, retain, and retrieve historical memories based on future narrative goals. We also introduce MiDramaBench, a bilingual benchmark for evaluating script logic and creative quality across different script lengths, together with causal-pattern metrics for narrative repetition and diversity. Experiments show consistent improvements across three backbone LLMs. For 60-episode scripts of up to 60k words, DraMaze reduces causal-pattern repetition by 32.1% and achieves a Logic score of 82.5, outperforming the best-performing baseline by 8.5 points.
